broad_paper_summary_limitation: The paper-level workbook effect pools the 2002 supra-natural and 2004 natural-range years.
evidence_basis: Primary study manipulates gelsemine as nectar defence and measures pollinators and nectar robbers in the same Gelsemium system.

broad_paper_summary_limitation: The paper-level workbook effect combines effective bird pollinators with morphologically mismatched birds and honey bees.
evidence_basis: Primary study shows dark phenolic nectar repels unwanted nectarivores while effective short-billed bird pollinators are comparatively unaffected.

broad_paper_summary_limitation: The paper-level workbook effect combines a legitimate bee response with a Lepidoptera antagonist response.
evidence_basis: Primary study treats milkweed cardenolides as herbivore defences and measures bumblebee foraging and monarch responses in the same study.

broad_paper_summary_limitation: The paper-level workbook effect collapses 21 dose-by-sugar contrasts from six colonies.
evidence_basis: Primary source states that plant secondary metabolites used for herbivore defence occur in nectar and reports dose- and sugar-dependent nicotine deterrence.

broad_paper_summary_limitation: The paper-level workbook effect pools visit number with visit length and averages natural-range and highly elevated alkaloid concentrations.
evidence_basis: Primary study shows no behavioural difference at 0-1 microgram per microlitre and strong reductions only at 2-4 micrograms per microlitre around 50 times natural nectar.

broad_paper_summary_limitation: The paper-level workbook effect combines infection states and two alkaloid preference experiments.
evidence_basis: Primary study tests parasite-mediated self-medication and bee health; it does not establish a flower-specific antagonist-reduction role for the focal treatments.

broad_paper_summary_limitation: The paper-level workbook effect combines compounds, microbes, bees, birds and other floral visitors.
evidence_basis: Primary study finds compound-specific microbial inhibition but concludes the compounds are unlikely to provide an effective general defence preserving nectar sugars.

broad_paper_summary_limitation: The paper-level workbook effect collapses multiple caffeine concentrations and assay panels.
evidence_basis: Primary study shows caffeine enhances memory at natural nectar concentrations below the bitter-taste threshold; it does not verify a flower-specific antagonist-reduction function.

broad_paper_summary_limitation: The workbook label conflicts with the probable primary source and the paper-level effect combines bee taxa with opposite responses.
evidence_basis: Year trait species design and response pattern match Tiedeken et al 2016; preserve the original workbook label and treat the source mapping as provisional pending exact row-to-figure verification.
